label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `exportReport` function does not handle errors thrown during the fetch request (e.g., failed exports), so the `busy` state remains `true` indefinitely. The fix should wrap the `exportReport` call in a `.catch()` to reset `busy` to `false` when an error occurs, ensuring the button is re-enabled.

input.title: Re-enable the export button after a failed export
input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `handleClick` function in the `ExportButton` component sets `busy` to `true` at the start of the export process but only resets it to `false` in the `.then()` callback, which only executes if the export succeeds. If the export fails (e.g., due to a non-2xx response), the `busy` state remains `true`, disabling the button. To fix this, the `.catch()` block should also reset `busy` to `false` to re-enable the button after a failed export.

File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `handleClick` function in the `ExportButton` component sets `busy` to `true` at the start of the export process but only resets it to `false` in the `.then()` callback, which only executes if the export succeeds. If the export fails (e.g., due to a non-2xx response), the `busy` state remains `true`, disabling the button. To fix this, the `.catch()` block should also reset `busy` to `false` to re-enable the button after a failed export.
